name: pulse-api-contract
description: Designs TypeScript public APIs for React components in this Laravel Inertia app. Use when defining props, callbacks, controlled/uncontrolled state, slots, compound components, discriminated unions, variants, or public behaviour contracts.
purpose: Prevent prop sprawl, implementation leaks, and unclear public behaviour.
single_responsibility: The public TypeScript API of a reusable React component: prop types, callback contracts, controlled/uncontrolled state, slots, and compound-component composition.
triggers: Component exposes public or reusable props, callbacks, or slots
Adding variants, compound parts, or asChild/polymorphic rendering
Designing controlled, uncontrolled, or hybrid component state
Changing shared component props consumed by other code
completion_criteria: Props are typed, descriptive, and have intentional defaults
Callbacks are named by public event with stable, documented payloads
Controlled, uncontrolled, or hybrid state is decided
Slot, children, asChild, and compound-part contracts are defined where needed
No DOM structure, classes, timing constants, or private state leak through the API
validation_criteria: The API supports the required behaviour without exposing internals
Accessibility and testing needs are representable through the API
Variants and discriminated unions are finite and typed
Documentation notes are ready when the component is reusable
failure_handling: If the required behaviour cannot be expressed without leaking internals or causing prop sprawl, stop and report the API tension instead of shipping a sprawling or unstable contract.
Report any prop, callback, or composition decision left unresolved because consumers or requirements are unknown.
escalation_path: Route uncertain Radix, polymorphic, or third-party library API behaviour through pulse-docs-research.
Escalate to the user when reuse scope, consumers, or a breaking API change require a scope or product decision.
Hand state-machine and effect concerns to pulse-state-effects and behaviour scenarios to pulse-tdd-planning.
responsibilities: Choose controlled, uncontrolled, or hybrid state.
Define slot, `children`, `asChild`, and compound component contracts.
Keep polymorphic and compound APIs narrow enough that accessibility and TypeScript inference remain understandable.
non_responsibilities: Test code, though tests should validate the contract.
